sections.title: How does the On-base plus slugging (ops) calculator work?
sections.html:
The On-base plus slugging (ops) calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports hit by pitch (HBP) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the singles (1B), the triples (3B), the walks (BB) and the sacrifice flies (SF).

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the On-base plus slugging (ops) calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Hit by pitch (HBP)=(-at bats (AB) × on-base percentage (OBP) − walks (BB) × on-base percentage (OBP) + walks (BB) + hits (H) − on-base percentage (OBP) × sacrifice flies (SF)) ÷ (on-base percentage (OBP) − 1)
Doubles (2B)=-2 × home runs (HR) + (1 ÷ 2) × total bases (TB) − 1 ÷ 2 × singles (1B) − 3 ÷ 2 × triples (3B)
At bats (AB)=total bases (TB) ÷ slugging percentage (SLG)
Slugging percentage (SLG)=-on-base percentage (OBP) + on-base plus slugging (OPS)
At bats (AB)=hits (H) ÷ batting average (BA)
Doubles (2B)=hits (H) − home runs (HR) − singles (1B) − triples (3B)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Take Singles (1B) = 10, Triples (3B) = 10, Home runs (HR) = 10 and Total bases (TB) = 10. The calculator returns Hits (H) = -5 and Doubles (2B) = -35.

The point of the example is the scale, not the particular digits: swap in your own figures and the same relationship produces your answer.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Hits (H) = -5 and Doubles (2B) = -35 should be roughly the size you expected from Singles (1B) = 10 and Triples (3B) = 10.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The On-base plus slugging (ops) calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Comparing two athletes or two attempts fairly
  • Tracking progress across a training block
  • Planning a session around a target you already know
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the singles, the triples and the walks — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the On-base plus slugging (ops) calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns hit by pitch (HBP), derived from the singles, the triples and the walks. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the On-base plus slugging (ops) calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the singles, the triples, the walks and the sacrifice flies, which is 8 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Hits (H) = -5. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the On-base plus slugging (ops) calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
